name: verify-tools
// tags: type:tooling since OR-35: the production preflight (tools/verify/preflight) runs the ecs-core domain through tools/seed/load-domain.mjs, so this project reads the typed core the way seed-tools does
// test: The runners here (the initial-bundle guard, the P0 proofs) keep their pure parts in node:test specs, so `test` is node's own runner rather than vitest; the runners themselves need a build or the emulators and run as `pnpm run verify:bundle` and `pnpm run verify:p0`. Its inputs reach past tools/verify because the preflight's spec reads the repository: the functions' source (P7's and P8's real-tree pins), firebase.json and package.json (the deploy wiring), tools/seed/load-domain.mjs (imported by the preflight), firestore.indexes.json (the audit-index spec's pins, tools/verify/indexes, and the retention spec's TTL groups, tools/verify/ops), tools/ops (the backstop scripts, their names.env — also read by the preflight's P9 — and the alert policies, which the ops spec dry-runs and pins), libs/ecs-core/src/primitives/log-event.data.ts (every metric's message must be one of its values), tools/seed/calendar.mjs (the seed instant's grammar, which the P0 seed-run spec reaches through load-domain.mjs — tools/verify/p0/seed-run.spec.mjs), the runbook (the runbook-gates spec pins its §4 blocks, tools/verify/runbook-gates), the CI workflow and its actions, the e2e specs with their support files, both Playwright configs, apps/web's project.json and tsconfigs, tsconfig.base.json and @playwright/test (the CI specs pin them, and the screenshot-tag spec lists the suite through Playwright's own loader, tools/verify/ci) and the TypeScript compiler P7 and P8 parse with — a cache keyed on tools/verify alone would replay a stale pass
// layering: Law 8 (CLAUDE.md): tier hierarchy, import cycles, tier barrels and the root-barrel ban in libs/ecs-core, deep relative imports across libs/apps/tools. It reads the whole workspace in about a second, so it is never cached: a cached pass could hide a new violation in a project it does not depend on
// runbook-gates: The runbook grep gates (docs/architecture/firestore-runbook.md §4) through their committed runner, tools/verify/runbook-gates/run-gates.mjs: it reads the blocks from the runbook at run time (the gates' only copy) and runs the §4.0 preamble plus each block alone. Never cached — the gates read the whole tree, untracked files included — and run alone, never beside a typecheck, lint or test: §4.9 writes a transient canary the other tasks would read. Pass --allow-dirty to run it on an uncommitted tree
